messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 63
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: Middle Eastern
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Auditor
  trauma_type: Trauma to a loved one
  pcl5: 63

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Locked Spaces: Being in a locked or confined room, Being in Nature: Being in a natural environment similar to where it happened, Victim Memories: Reminders of victims
  Threat: Avoid Unfamiliar Places: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger, Sleep Problems: Trouble falling or staying asleep, Hypervigilance: Being superalert or watchful or on guard
  Memory: Full Sensory Reliving: When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once, Terror on Recall: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time, Triggered Without Warning: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
  Negative Appraisals: Lost Faith: I have lost my faith in people, life, or a higher power, Body as Enemy: My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe, Helplessness: I can't stop bad things from happening to me

Vignette:
Sara, a 63-year-old Middle Eastern woman who works as an auditor, has been grappling with intense psychological distress following a traumatic event that involved her loved one. Sara’s life changed irrevocably on the day she received news of her nephew's tragic death in a hiking accident. The incident occurred in a remote forest where she and her family often went to spend weekends together. The memory of that day remains vivid and overwhelming for Sara, each detail etched into her mind with the clarity of a full sensory experience. Every time she recalls the event, it feels as though she is reliving every moment—she can hear the rustling of leaves, feel the chill in the air, and see the desolate forest path leading to where her nephew was found. The terror she felt that day comes rushing back whenever something triggers the memory, often without warning. Sara’s triggers are particularly potent due to their direct connection to the traumatic event. Being in a natural environment similar to where it happened can instantly bring back the full memory, leaving her feeling as if she is right there again. This has led her to avoid such environments altogether. Moreover, being in locked or confined spaces, like an office or any enclosed room, also triggers her memories and sends waves of anxiety through her. Her hypervigilance is a constant presence, making her superalert and watchful wherever she goes. She cannot shake the feeling that danger lurks around every corner, especially when she ventures into unfamiliar places. This fear has led her to avoid such environments entirely, confining herself to familiar settings where she feels safer. However, this avoidance has had significant consequences on both her personal life and career as an auditor. Sara’s sleep problems have also intensified over time. She often finds it difficult to fall asleep or stay asleep due to the intrusive thoughts and memories that keep her mind racing late into the night. Her body remains in a state of high alert even when she is physically safe, reacting as if she were still in danger. This has left her feeling increasingly helpless and unable to prevent bad things from happening. The loss of faith in people, life, and a higher power has compounded Sara’s distress. She feels that the world is an unpredictable and dangerous place where no one can be trusted or relied upon for support. Her body’s persistent reaction as if she were still in danger further reinforces her sense of helplessness and mistrust. Over the past few months, these symptoms have gradually eroded Sara's ability to function effectively at work. She has become increasingly isolated, avoiding social interactions and professional engagements that could trigger memories or anxiety. Her relationships with colleagues have also suffered as a result of her withdrawal and inability to fully engage in her duties. It was her sister’s persistent urging that finally brought Sara to seek help. Her sister recognized the depth of Sara’s distress and urged her to speak with someone who could provide support and guidance through this difficult time. Sara is most afraid of losing control and being unable to manage her reactions, but she also hopes for a sense of peace and stability in her life once again. In her current state, Sara feels overwhelmed by the fear that bad things will continue to happen uncontrollably. She is seeking help with the hope of regaining some semblance of normalcy and finding ways to cope more effectively with her memories and triggers.
